parts.name: Sediment filter
parts.note: Varies by maker and model. Use a shorter cycle with poor water quality or heavy use.
parts.source: Cuckoo purifier care schedule (rental retailer page): 4 months. For reference, Coway manual (CHP-7210N): Nanotrap filter 4 months (not the same filter type). No official sediment filter document found.

parts.name: Pre-carbon filter
parts.note: Can change with source water quality and usage.
parts.source: LG Electronics Korea support: replacement cycle by filter type

parts.name: UF membrane filter
parts.note: Can change with source water quality and usage.
parts.source: LG Electronics Korea support: replacement cycle by filter type

parts.name: RO membrane
parts.note: Varies by maker and model (18 to 24 months). It changes with source water and usage, so follow your product manual first.
parts.source: Coway water purifier manual (P-6320L): RO membrane filter, expected replacement 20 months

parts.name: Post-carbon filter
parts.note: Some models use 12 months.
parts.source: LG Electronics Korea support: replacement cycle by filter type

parts.name: HEPA filter
parts.note: Shorter with long daily use or polluted air. Replace it when the indicator lights up or the filter smells.
parts.source: LG Electronics Korea support (dust filter 12 months, 6 months on some models); Dyson support (12 months)

parts.name: Carbon (odor) filter
parts.note: Some models use a 6-month cycle.
parts.source: LG Electronics Korea support: air purifier filter care (odor filter 12 months, 6 months on some models)

parts.name: Pre-filter cleaning
parts.note: This is a cleaning cycle, not a replacement. Clean it more often in dusty rooms.
parts.source: LG Electronics Korea support: air purifier filter care (wash the mesh filter once a month; some models as needed)

parts.name: AC filter cleaning
parts.note: During the cooling season. Also clean it before and after summer.
parts.source: Samsung Electronics Service Korea: clean the panel and filter about every 2 weeks

parts.name: Engine oil and filter
parts.note: Varies by model and engine (Hyundai normal schedule: 10,000 to 15,000 km or 12 months; US: 8,000 mi or 12 months). Severe use (short trips, heavy traffic) needs 5,000 to 7,500 km or 6 months.
parts.source: Hyundai owner's manuals: normal maintenance schedule (DN8 2025 US/AU, SX2 2025 Korea), severe usage (DN8 2026 Korea)

parts.name: Cabin air filter
parts.note: Varies by model and region (12 to 24 months). Replace it more often on dusty roads.
parts.source: Hyundai owner's manuals: normal maintenance schedule (SX2 2025 Korea 12 months, DN8 2025 Australia 24 months)

parts.name: Engine air filter
parts.note: Varies by model and region (36 to 48 months, about 40,000 km). Inspect it often in dusty areas.
parts.source: Hyundai owner's manuals: normal maintenance schedule (DN8 2025 Australia 48 months/40,000 km, US 36 months/24,000 mi)

parts.name: Brake fluid
parts.note: Varies by model and region (Australia 30,000 km or 24 months, Korea 50,000 km, US 48 months).
parts.source: Hyundai owner's manuals: normal maintenance schedule (DN8 2025 Australia/US, SX2 2025 Korea)

parts.name: Engine coolant
parts.note: On a new car, first replace at 200,000 km or 120 months, then every 40,000 km or 24 months (Hyundai).
parts.source: Hyundai owner's manuals: normal maintenance schedule (DN8 2025 Australia/US)

parts.name: Tire rotation
parts.note: The US manual says 8,000 mi (13,000 km) or 12 months.
parts.source: Hyundai owner's manual: normal maintenance schedule (DN8 2025 Australia)

parts.name: Car battery
parts.note: Shorter in hot climates. After 3 years, have it tested every year.
parts.source: AAA: replace every three to five years as a general rule

parts.name: Wiper blades
parts.note: 6 to 12 months, depending on climate and driving. Replace them now if they streak or chatter.
parts.source: AAA: replace every 6 to 12 months

parts.name: Toothbrush
parts.note: Replace it sooner if the bristles are frayed.
parts.source: American Dental Association (ADA): every 3 to 4 months

parts.name: Electric toothbrush head
parts.note: Based on brushing twice a day. Replace it sooner when the indicator bristles fade.
parts.source: Philips Sonicare and Oral-B support: about every 3 months

parts.name: Shower filter
parts.note: For cartridge filters (about 10,000 gallons or 6 months). Small vitamin or sediment filters can be much shorter, so follow the label first.
parts.source: Aquasana: shower cartridge lasts 10,000 gallons or up to 6 months

parts.name: Humidifier wick filter
parts.note: For wicking (evaporative) filters: 30 to 60 days. Replace it more often with hard water.
parts.source: Honeywell: change the wicking filter every 30 to 60 days

parts.name: Refrigerator water filter
parts.note: Use genuine filters.
parts.source: Samsung support (every 6 months); LG Electronics Korea support (dispenser fridge filter 6 months)

parts.name: Range hood filter cleaning
parts.note: For metal mesh grease filters. Clean them more often if you fry or stir-fry a lot. Replace carbon filters; do not wash them.
parts.source: Broan-NuTone support: wash about every month; Faber: every 2 months

parts.name: Vacuum filter wash
parts.note: For cordless vacuums. Let it dry fully for at least 24 hours.
parts.source: Dyson support: wash the cordless vacuum filter once a month

parts.name: Kitchen sponge
parts.note: Replace it now if it smells or looks dirty. University of Illinois Extension advises switching sponges and dish rags for clean ones every day and washing or sanitizing them.
parts.source: News interview with a Cleveland Clinic infectious disease specialist (at least every 2 weeks). No official institution document found.

parts.name: Pillow
parts.note: By fill: memory foam 2 to 3 years, latex 2 to 4 years, down or feather 1 to 3 years, polyester 6 months to 2 years. Replace it if it stays folded when you fold it in half. Wash pillowcases weekly.
parts.source: Sleep Foundation: most experts recommend replacing pillows every 1 to 2 years

parts.name: Mattress rotation
parts.note: For foam, latex and newer innerspring mattresses. Older innerspring: 2 to 6 months. Some mattresses must not be rotated, so check the manual first.
parts.source: Sleep Foundation: mattress care

parts.name: Smoke alarm test
parts.note: Push the test button and listen for the alarm.
parts.source: U.S. Fire Administration (USFA): test the alarm monthly

parts.name: Smoke alarm battery
parts.note: For replaceable batteries (9-volt and similar). Alarms with a sealed 10-year battery need a new alarm instead.
parts.source: U.S. Fire Administration (USFA): replace the batteries at least once every year

parts.name: Smoke alarm unit
parts.note: Count 10 years from the manufacture date, not the purchase date.
parts.source: U.S. Fire Administration (USFA): replace the entire smoke alarm every 10 years

parts.name: Fire extinguisher check
parts.note: Look at the gauge (needle in the green), the safety pin and the body. Replace or service it according to the label and local rules.
parts.source: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.157: inspect portable extinguishers visually every month

parts.name: Pet fountain filter
parts.note: Replace it more often with several pets. Clean the fountain on the same cycle.
parts.source: PetSafe support: replace the filter every 2 to 4 weeks

parts.name: Drive belt inspection
parts.note: This is an inspection cycle, not a replacement. Replace the belt if it is cracked or stretched.
parts.source: Hyundai owner's manual: normal maintenance schedule (DN8 2025 Australia), inspect every 30,000 km or 24 months

parts.name: Tire replacement (age)
parts.note: Rubber ages even without wear. Count from the manufacture date (last 4 digits of the DOT code = week and year). After 5 years, have the tires inspected every year. Replace them sooner if the tread is worn to the limit.
parts.source: Coverage of the NHTSA tire aging report: some vehicle makers say 6 years, tire makers up to 10 years. Agency original not confirmed.

parts.name: Water pitcher filter
parts.note: About 40 gallons or 2 months, whichever comes first. Replace it more often with hard water or heavy use.
parts.source: Brita: replace every 40 gallons or about every 2 months

parts.name: Washer tub cleaning
parts.note: If you skipped it for 6 months or more, run it 3 times in a row. Front loaders: run Tub Clean after about 30 washes or when tCL appears.
parts.source: LG Electronics Korea support: clean the top-load washer tub once a month

parts.name: Bed sheet washing
parts.note: If you do not sleep in the bed every day, every 2 weeks can be enough. If pets sleep in the bed, wash every 3 to 4 days.
parts.source: Sleep Foundation: most people should wash sheets once a week

parts.name: Mattress replacement
parts.note: Replace it sooner if it sags, gets noisy, or you wake up stiff. Latex can last more than 8 years.
parts.source: Sleep Foundation: replace mattresses every 6 to 8 years under normal conditions

parts.name: Humidifier tank cleaning
parts.note: Empty the tank, wipe it dry and refill it every day. Rinse well after any cleaning agent.
parts.source: US EPA: clean portable humidifiers every third day, change the water daily

parts.name: Contact lens case
parts.note: Get a new case at least every 3 months. Rinse it with solution daily and store it upside down with the caps off.
parts.source: US CDC: replace your contact lens case at least every 3 months

parts.name: CO alarm test
parts.note: Replace the batteries once a year. Replace the unit as the maker says or when the end-of-life signal sounds.
parts.source: US CPSC: test alarms monthly, replace batteries annually

parts.name: Fire extinguisher replacement
parts.note: For dry chemical extinguishers in Korea, counted from the manufacture date. Rules differ by country; follow the label and local rules.
parts.source: Korea Fire Institute (KFI): dry chemical extinguishers past 10 years from manufacture must be replaced or performance-checked

parts.name: AC outdoor unit cleaning
parts.note: Clear the area around the unit and remove dust from the coil before summer. Turn the power off first.
parts.source: Carrier says to deep clean the indoor coils and the outdoor condenser at least once a year

parts.name: AC deep cleaning
parts.note: The coils and fan need professional tools. Book earlier if you smell odor or cooling is weak.
parts.source: Carrier says to deep clean the indoor coils and the outdoor condenser at least once a year. LG offers a disassembly cleaning service but gives no interval

parts.name: Water purifier sanitizing
parts.note: On hot and cold models, run the hot water sanitizing cycle for the spout. Discard the hot water.
parts.source: LG Electronics support: sanitize the spout every 3 months (PuriCare dual purifier). The water pipe self-sanitizes weekly

parts.name: Air purifier sensor cleaning
parts.note: Unplug the unit and open the sensor cover. Wipe the lens with a damp cotton swab, then dry it with a dry swab.
parts.source: LG Electronics support: clean the PM1.0 sensor once every two months

parts.name: Robot vacuum filter
parts.note: Tap the filter often and keep it dry. The interval varies by model; replace it when it shows wear.
parts.source: iRobot support: replace the filter every 3-6 months (Roomba 100/1000). Roborock manual: washable filter every 6-12 months

parts.name: Robot vacuum side brush
parts.note: Remove tangled hair monthly. Replace the brush when the bristles bend or wear.
parts.source: iRobot support (edge sweeping brush) 3-6 months; Roborock manual 3-6 months

parts.name: Robot vacuum main brush
parts.note: Cut away wrapped hair. Replace sooner if the brush is noisy or worn.
parts.source: iRobot support 6-12 months; Roborock manual 6-12 months

parts.name: Robot vacuum mop pad
parts.note: Wash and dry it after use. Replace it when it smells or the fibers wear out.
parts.source: iRobot support 3-6 months (Roomba 100/1000); Roborock manual 1-3 months

parts.name: Vacuum cleaner dust bag
parts.note: Replace the bag at once when the full light turns on. Replace it if it smells, even earlier.
parts.source: LG Electronics support: replace the dust bag of the LG Compact Tower dust-emptying dock within 1-2 months

parts.name: Dehumidifier dust filter cleaning
parts.note: Remove dust with a vacuum or soft brush. If very dirty, wash with mild soap and water under 40 C.
parts.source: LG Electronics support: clean the micro filter (dust net) once a month

parts.name: Washing machine gasket cleaning
parts.note: Wipe with warm water and oxygen bleach, then leave the door open to dry. Do not use chlorine bleach.
parts.source: LG Electronics support: clean the rubber gasket monthly with oxygen bleach

parts.name: Washing machine drain filter cleaning
parts.note: Drain the tub, turn the filter out and rinse off debris. Check first that no hot water is left.
parts.source: Samsung (US): clean the pump filter at least monthly or about every 40 washes. Samsung (Canada): every 1-3 months. LG says only to clean it regularly

parts.name: Dryer exhaust duct cleaning
parts.note: Clean more often if you dry often or drying takes longer. A professional gives a safer, deeper clean.
parts.source: Samsung (Canada): inspect the exhaust vent at least once a year, more often with frequent use

parts.name: Dishwasher filter cleaning
parts.note: Clean it sooner after heavy food soil, odors, or slow draining.
parts.source: Bosch UK support: clean the filter at least every 2 weeks. Samsung support (Levant page): clean every 2-4 weeks.

parts.name: Dishwasher self-clean cycle
parts.note: Run the cleaning programme with the machine empty. If your model has none, follow its manual.
parts.source: Bosch UK support: run a cleaning programme at least every 2 months.

parts.name: Refrigerator condenser coil cleaning
parts.note: Unplug the fridge and remove dust with a vacuum or brush. Do it more often with pets.
parts.source: Samsung service Korea: clean the machine compartment about once a year (seen in search summary, page not opened). Bosch UK support: clean the coils every 6-12 months.

parts.name: Electric kettle descaling
parts.note: Descale more often with hard water or heavy use. Follow the maker's method.
parts.source: Several household guides say about once a month (seen in search summaries only; no maker figure found).

parts.name: Coffee machine descaling
parts.note: Use a shorter cycle with hard water or heavy use. Follow the machine's alert if it has one.
parts.source: Nespresso Korea FAQ: every 6 months at about 40 cups per week. Nespresso US FAQ: every 3 months or 300 capsules, whichever is first.

parts.name: Coffee machine water filter
parts.note: Use a shorter cycle with hard water or heavy use. Brita cartridges use a 4-week limit.
parts.source: De'Longhi FAQ: filter lasts 2 months under normal conditions. Brita UK FAQ: replace a MAXTRA PRO cartridge at least every 4 weeks.

parts.name: Rice cooker rubber gasket
parts.note: Replace it right away if steam leaks or the lid feels stiff. Packings are model-specific.
parts.source: CUCKOO America help center: every 2-3 years (seen in search summary, page not opened). One Cuckoo model manual: 12 months (retailer listing summary).

parts.name: Food waste dryer filter
parts.note: Cycle varies by model. Replace sooner if odor returns.
parts.source: Smart Kara product page: carbon filter up to 6 months (search summary). Comparison blog: 3-4 months. No per-model official document opened.

parts.name: Nonstick frying pan
parts.note: Replace it at once if the coating peels or is deeply scratched.
parts.source: Cookware and Bakeware Alliance spokesperson (via America's Test Kitchen): 5-7 years for a quality coating.

parts.name: Dishcloth and kitchen towel
parts.note: Swap it right away after wiping raw meat juice. Wash on a hot machine cycle.
parts.source: University of Minnesota Extension: replace dishcloths daily (search summary; page blocked). USDA FSIS: wash dishcloths often on the hot cycle.

parts.name: Bidet nozzle tip
parts.note: Varies by model. Check your maker's guidance.
parts.source: Coway rental retailer page: nozzle tip 2 or 4 months. No official manual found.

parts.name: Bidet water filter
parts.note: Choose the genuine filter for your model number.
parts.source: Coway rental retailer page: pre-micro filter 4 months. Comparison blog: 4-6 months. No official manual found.

parts.name: Bath towel
parts.note: Wash two to three times a week in humid homes or summer.
parts.source: Cleveland Clinic: launder or swap bath towels at least once a week.

parts.name: Shower pouf and loofah
parts.note: Natural loofah 3-4 weeks, plastic pouf up to 2 months. Discard at once if mold or musty smell appears.
parts.source: Cleveland Clinic: natural loofah 3-4 weeks, plastic 2 months.

parts.name: Shower curtain liner
parts.note: You can also machine-rinse it with vinegar or bleach instead of replacing.
parts.source: Cleveland Clinic dermatologist: replace the shower liner every 6 months to a year.

parts.name: Bath mat
parts.note: Check the care label before washing. Dry it fully.
parts.source: Bathroom cleaning guides (Angi etc.): at least weekly; another says monthly (search summaries). No agency source found.

parts.name: Bathroom exhaust fan cleaning
parts.note: Turn off power and wipe dust off the grille.
parts.source: Korean lifestyle article (WikiTree): wipe the grille about once a month (search summary). No official source.

parts.name: Razor blade cartridge
parts.note: About 20 shaves for 5-blade, 15 for 3-blade. Replace sooner if it tugs or irritates.
parts.source: Gillette US: every 5-10 shaves; daily shavers about weekly; Fusion5/ProGlide about 20 shaves.

parts.name: Hairbrush
parts.note: Replace at once if bristles bend, fall out, or the base cracks. Remove hair every 1-2 weeks.
parts.source: Dermatologist quoted in articles: replace every 6 months; general guides 6-12 months (search summaries).

parts.name: Makeup sponge
parts.note: AAD says clean after every use. Replace at once if it tears or smells.
parts.source: American Academy of Dermatology: clean sponges after every use (no replacement interval). 1-3 months replacement comes from beauty media summaries.

parts.name: Makeup brush cleaning
parts.note: Rinse only the tips with mild shampoo and dry flat.
parts.source: American Academy of Dermatology: wash makeup brushes every 7 to 10 days.

parts.name: Mascara
parts.note: Discard at once if it dries out. Throw away the product used during an eye infection.
parts.source: AAD: mascara lasts three months. US FDA: manufacturers usually recommend discarding it 2-4 months after purchase.

parts.name: Comforter and blanket washing
parts.note: With a duvet cover or top sheet, wash the comforter once or twice a year. Wash it every 3 to 6 months without a cover, or with allergies, pets or heavy sweating. Wash the cover every 1 to 2 weeks.
parts.source: Sleep Foundation: once or twice a year with a cover or top sheet; every 3 to 6 months without a cover, or with allergies, pets or heavy sweating; cover every 1 to 2 weeks. The page covers comforters; no blanket-specific figure was found.

parts.name: Comforter replacement
parts.note: This figure is for down comforters. Synthetic fill loses loft faster. Replace sooner if it clumps, smells or no longer keeps you warm.
parts.source: Sleep Foundation: down comforters can last 10 to 15 years or longer with proper care

parts.name: Microfiber cleaning cloth
parts.note: These are the maker's guarantee periods, so a cloth used daily may wear out sooner. Rinse and wring it, wash it weekly, and avoid bleach and fabric softener.
parts.source: E-Cloth care page: General Purpose Cloth has a 3-year or 300-wash guarantee. Some product pages by the same company say 1 year or 100 washes, so the range covers both.

parts.name: Door lock batteries
parts.note: Check the batteries for leaks every 6 months. When the low-battery alert sounds, replace all batteries at once. Battery life is about 10 to 12 months at 10 uses a day.
parts.source: Samsung digital door lock manuals (SHP-DP728, DP738, DP940 and others): check batteries about every 6 months. Seen only in manual copies, not on an official Samsung page; it varies by model.

parts.name: PC dust cleaning
parts.note: Casual use needs a cleaning twice a year. In dusty rooms, or with pets or indoor smoking, clean every 2 to 3 months. Power off and unplug first, then blow out the dust with compressed air.
parts.source: Corsair (PC parts maker) dust guide: every 3 to 6 months in general, twice a year for casual users, every 2 to 3 months in dusty places

parts.name: Silicone caulk replacement
parts.note: Use the short end in damp places such as bathrooms. Replace it at once if it cracks, peels or grows mold that will not clean off.
parts.source: Duravit (sanitary ware maker): replace silicone joints after about 5 to 8 years, sooner if brittle, cracked or moldy

parts.name: Earth leakage breaker test
parts.note: Press the TEST button on the breaker in the distribution box. If the switch trips, it works. If it does not trip or will not reset, have a professional replace it.
parts.source: Korean Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Energy press release (2007, via korea.kr): test about once a month. A Korea Electrical Safety Corporation tip (via Boannews) also says monthly, and replace the breaker if it does not trip.

parts.name: Gas safety inspection visit
parts.note: The gas supplier must inspect your gas-use facilities at least once every 6 months. Allow the visit and ask them to check for leaks, hoses and joints.
parts.source: Korea Gas Safety Corporation: gas suppliers must inspect customers' gas-use facilities at least once every 6 months

parts.name: Emergency kit check
parts.note: Replace expired items and update the kit for your family's needs. Some guidance checks water, food and batteries every 6 months, so the range covers that.
parts.source: Ready.gov: replace expired items and rethink your needs every year. The 6-month check comes from archived CDC guidance, seen only in a search summary.

parts.name: Baby bottle teat
parts.note: Pull the teat in all directions before each use. Replace it at once if it is cracked, stretched or sticky, whatever its age.
parts.source: Philips Avent: replace teats every 3 months, sooner if damaged. Chicco: roughly every 2 months.

parts.name: Plastic baby bottle
parts.note: This is for plastic bottles. Glass bottles have no set interval. Replace either type at once if it shows scratches, cracks or leaks.
parts.source: Chicco (maker) blog: replace plastic bottles every 4 to 6 months as a safe rule of thumb

parts.name: Pacifier
parts.note: Pull it in all directions before each use. If it is damaged in any way, replace it before the 4 weeks are up.
parts.source: Philips Avent support: replace the pacifier after 4 weeks of use for safety and hygiene, and sooner if damaged

parts.name: Car seat expiry
parts.note: Count from the manufacture date, not the purchase date. Find the exact expiry date on the label under the seat or on its shell and adjust this reminder to it. Replace a seat after a crash.
parts.source: Safe Kids Worldwide: usually 6 to 10 years. Chicco: many range from 5 to 10 years, and the date is on the seat label.

parts.name: Reduction gear oil check (EV)
parts.note: Hyundai lists a reducer fluid inspection every 48 months or 52,000 km on the IONIQ 5 family. Under severe use the fluid is replaced every 120,000 km.
parts.source: Hyundai owner's manual, normal maintenance schedule (IONIQ 5 NE1N 2026 US): reducer fluid marked I at 48/96/144 months (32,000/64,000/96,000 mi), i.e. every 48 months or 32,000 mi (about 52,000 km); severe-use page: replace every 80,000 mi (120,000 km)

parts.name: High-voltage battery coolant check (EV)
parts.note: A water-cooled high-voltage battery needs a coolant amount and cooling system check every 12 months or 13,000 km. Coolant is replaced at 120 months, then every 24 months. Use a dealer.
parts.source: Hyundai owner's manual, EV special care schedule (IONIQ 5 NE1N 2026 US): water-cooled coolant amount, EWP and 3-way valve marked I every 12 months or 8,000 mi (13,000 km)

parts.name: High-voltage battery inspection (EV)
parts.note: Check the high-voltage battery insulation resistance and voltage deviation every 12 months or 13,000 km. An authorized service center does this check.
parts.source: Hyundai owner's manual, EV special care schedule (IONIQ 5 NE1N 2026 US): high-voltage battery insulation resistance and voltage deviation marked I every 12 months or 8,000 mi (13,000 km)

parts.name: Washer fluid top-up
parts.note: Check the washer fluid level at least once a month and top up with commercial washer fluid. In bad weather, check at every fuel stop.
parts.source: Honda owner's manual: check the windshield washer reservoir at least monthly in normal use (seen only in a search summary; the PDF did not open)

parts.name: Periodic vehicle inspection
parts.note: A private passenger car needs an inspection every 2 years. A new car's first inspection is due 5 years after registration (table revised 2024-12). Late inspection carries a fine.
parts.source: Gangdong-gu Office guide quoting the Enforcement Rule of the Motor Vehicle Management Act, Annex 15-2 (rev. 2024-12-17): private passenger car validity 2 years, first inspection of a new car 5 years

parts.name: Dash cam memory card replacement
parts.note: Replace a dash cam card about every 18 months to 2 years. Format it in the camera every 2-3 weeks to cut errors.
parts.source: Nextbase (dash cam maker) support: replace the SD card about every 18 months to 2 years; format every 2-3 weeks for most users

parts.name: Wheel alignment check
parts.note: Check every 6 to 12 months. Check right away after a curb or pothole hit, new tires, or if the car pulls to one side.
parts.source: Firestone service pages: every 6,000 mi or six months, at least once a year (service provider advice, not a vehicle maker figure)

parts.name: Tire pressure check
parts.note: Check all tires, including the spare, at least once a month when they are cold. A pressure warning light does not replace a gauge check.
parts.source: Hyundai owner's manual, Tires and wheels (MEa 2026): check your tires at least once a month

parts.name: Motorcycle engine oil
parts.note: It depends on the model. The Honda Shadow 750 says 12,800 km or 12 months and the Yamaha TW200 says 6,000 km or 6 months. Follow whichever comes first.
parts.source: Honda VT750 owner's manual: every 8,000 mi (12,800 km) or 12 months; Yamaha TW200 manual: 6,000 km or 6 months (manualslib summary)

parts.name: Motorcycle chain clean and lube
parts.note: The Honda off-road CRF450L says inspect and lubricate every 500 km or 3 months. Road models usually say every 800-1,000 km, and after rain.
parts.source: Honda CRF450L owner's manual: chain inspect and lubricate every 500 km or 3 months (table partly decoded); Yamaha and Honda road models 800-1,000 km

parts.name: Motorcycle brake fluid
parts.note: Replace every 2 years. Replace the master cylinder and caliper seals at the same time.
parts.source: Yamaha MT-03 owner's manual (Europe): change brake fluid every 2 years; Honda Hornet owner's manual: 2 years

parts.name: Motorcycle coolant
parts.note: Change the coolant every 3 years on a liquid-cooled motorcycle. This does not apply to air-cooled models.
parts.source: Yamaha MT-03 owner's manual (Europe): change coolant every 3 years; Honda Hornet owner's manual: 3 years

parts.name: Bicycle helmet
parts.note: Replace at once after a crash or if you see cracks or damage. Makers differ: 3 years or 5 years.
parts.source: Smith: replace every 5 years. Trek: replace after 3 years even if undamaged. Bicycle Helmet Safety Institute: most makers now say 5 years.

parts.name: Bicycle cables and housing
parts.note: Usually done in spring. Replace sooner if the lever feels stiff, shifting is slow, or you see rust.
parts.source: Shimano tune-up guide: the average rider should replace cables and housing once a year, preferably in spring. (Seen in search summary only; the page itself could not be opened.)

parts.name: Hydraulic brake fluid
parts.note: Yearly for DOT fluid, every two years for mineral oil. Do it more often with frequent or aggressive riding.
parts.source: SRAM brake service guide: bleed DOT fluid brakes at least once a year; mineral oil brakes only every two years.

parts.name: Cat litter full change
parts.note: Daily scooping lets you wait longer. Change sooner with more cats or if the litter stops clumping.
parts.source: Purina UK: full change weekly for clumping litter (one cat). Dr. Elsey's: totally change litter every 3-4 weeks depending on use.

parts.name: Cat litter box
parts.note: Scratches in plastic hold odor and bacteria. Replace sooner if you see scratches, cracks, or stains.
parts.source: Petco experts: replace a typical plastic box about once a year. Dr. Elsey's: every 6 to 12 months. (Seen in search summaries only; pages not confirmed.)

parts.name: Litter box carbon filter
parts.note: Change more often with heavy use or scented litter. Use the filter that fits your model.
parts.source: Litter-Robot FAQ: change the carbon filter every month for best odor absorption; depends on use. No official interval found for other brands (e.g. Catit).

parts.name: Aquarium filter cartridge
parts.note: Change sooner if water flow clearly drops. Replacing all media at once removes helpful bacteria.
parts.source: Tetra aquarium guide: change the filter cartridge at least every four weeks, or when water flow drops noticeably.

parts.name: Aquarium partial water change
parts.note: Change about 25% of the water each time. Use dechlorinated water at the same temperature.
parts.source: Tetra: change 25% of the water every two weeks. API: partial water change (25%) every two weeks.

parts.name: Pet bed
parts.note: Replace sooner if the filling is flat, the bed is torn, or your pet stops using it. Cheap beds wear out faster.
parts.source: Petco and pet retailer guides: usually 1 to 3 years. No official body found; retailer articles only.

parts.name: Pet food and water bowls (wash)
parts.note: Wash with soap and hot water. Replace cracked or scratched bowls because bacteria stay in them.
parts.source: US FDA: wash pet food bowls and scooping and measuring utensils with soap and hot water after each use. Treated as at least once a day.
